description:
The cross-surface gates are honestly documented per-benchmark, but the campaign
headline ("N benchmarks gated") hides that the gates are not equally strong
oracles. For DSL-generated benchmarks (SSB, ~40/43 ClickBench), both DataFrame
backends are generated from ONE spec, so the only independent signal is
SQL-vs-spec - a weaker check than SQL-vs-independent-handwritten-DataFrame (e.g.
CoffeeShop's hand-written impls). A reader who sees "guarded" may infer an
independent cross-check that, for several gates, does not exist.

Relatedly, the oracle coverage map already reports "guarded" on REGISTRATION, with
an Enforced column distinguishing enforced (CI-blocking) vs staged; surface the
independence dimension in the same table so "guarded" cannot be misread as
"independently verified".

preserves.behavior: Per-benchmark reference-independence docstrings remain; this surfaces them, not removes them.
The existing coverage-map drift guard (--check) stays green after regeneration.

drift-guard (--check) green after regeneration.
